We integrated and analyzed gene expression data of DN patients from multiple GEO databases and identified 33 differentially expressed ICGs. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that these genes are involved in immune response and inflammation-related pathways. Immune cell infiltration analysis indicated a significant increase in immune cell abundance in the kidneys of DN patients. CSF1R was consistently identified as a key gene using various methods, including LASSO regression, machine learning algorithms (GLM, RF, SVM, XGB), and WGCNA analysis focusing on both disease-related and cluster-related modules. The identification of CSF1R was further validated in an external dataset and single-cell RNA sequencing data. CSF1R was upregulated in DN patients and played a crucial role in regulating immune responses and inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed the involvement of CSF1R in renal fibrosis, indicating its potential as a therapeutic target for DN. This study provides valuable insights into the role of ICGs and CSF1R in the pathogenesis of DN and suggests their potential as targets for diagnosis and treatment.

title: NFE2L1 promotes cisplatin resistance by attenuating ferroptosis through SLC27A2-mediated fatty acid metabolism in ovarian cancer.
abstract: Approaches that promote ferroptosis have emerged as promising therapeutic strategies for chemotherapy-resistant cancers; however, the mechanisms regulating ferroptosis during acquired therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Using RNA sequencing, we identified that Nuclear Factor Erythroid-2 Related Factor 1 (NFE2L1) is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer (OC) cells and patient tissues, as well as in ferroptosis-resistant models. Genetic knockdown of NFE2L1 resensitized cells to cisplatin both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, this effect was largely reversed by ferroptosis inhibitors, which significantly rescued cell survival following NFE2L1 depletion under cisplatin treatment. Further experiments demonstrated that modulating NFE2L1 expression affects the response to ferroptosis inducers by regulating iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, NFE2L1 silencing increased the transcription of long-chain fatty acid transport protein 2 (SLC27A2/FATP2). Chromatin immunoprecipitation and dual-luciferase reporter assays showed that NFE2L1 bound directly to the SLC27A2 promoter, where it competitively inhibited the recruitment of the transcription factor SP1. As a key member of the long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase family, FATP2 promotes the uptake and activation of long-chain fatty acids, processes that have been implicated in the regulation of ferroptosis. Subsequent LC-MS-based lipidomic analysis revealed that NFE2L1 reprogrammed intracellular fatty acid metabolism, characterized by increased polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) levels and decreased monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA) levels within phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs), thereby increasing cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. Consistent with these findings, supplementation with exogenous unsaturated fatty acids modulated NFE2L1-mediated ferroptosis sensitivity. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel NFE2L1/SLC27A2 axis that drives cisplatin resistance in OC by suppressing ferroptosis, and suggest a potential therapeutic strategy for treating cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer.

title: RACK1 maintains mouse hematopoietic stem cells by directly binding to and stabilizing LDB1.
abstract: A core complex with transcription factors (TFs) TAL1/TCF3/GATA2 and adaptors LMO2/LDB1 lies at the top of the hematopoietic transcriptional hierarchy. The mechanism(s) underlying the expression of these components remain elusive. Adaptor RACK1 interacts with multiple TFs and modulates their activation and/or stability. However, a role of RACK1 in the transcriptional control of hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) fates hasn't been disclosed. Here, we report that RACK1 is expressed across various hematopoietic cell types. Adulthood Rack1 deletion in type I interferon- (IFN-I)-responsive cells leads to rapid and profound hematopoietic failure and HSC loss. HSC exhaustion upon adulthood Rack1 deletion results from cell-intrinsic defects with massive apoptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing indicates that adulthood Rack1 deletion in IFN-I-responsive cells leads to aberrant lineage-geneset-scores of transcriptional HSCs and the emergence of stressed HSCs. Furthermore, prenatal deletion of Rack1 in hematopoietic cells results in reduced and defective HSCs in the fetal liver. Mechanistically, RACK1 prevents HSC loss through maintaining the protein level of LDB1. The direct interaction between RACK1 and LDB1 suppressing its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation, thereby stabilizes LDB1. Therefore, RACK1 maintains adult and fetal mouse HSCs through, at least partially, directly binding to and stabilizing LDB1.

title: The small protein PhrS-P, encoded by the dual-function small RNA PhrS, augments fitness of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the presence of aminoglycosides.
abstract: PhrS (Pseudomonas Hfq-binding RNA S) is a dual-function small RNA of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The base-pairing small regulatory RNA PhrS-R positively regulates pyocyanin biosynthesis. PhrS-R stimulates the production of the Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) by indirectly activating the translation of pqsR mRNA, encoding the quorum sensing regulator PqsR (MvfR), and by inhibiting the synthesis of the anthranilate degradation regulator AntR. Furthermore, PhrS-R was shown to promote biofilm formation, swarming motility and CRISPR-Cas immunity. In addition, PhrS encodes a 37 amino acid long and conserved small protein (PhrS-P), the function of which remained unknown. Here, we provide evidence that PhrS-P is an inner membrane protein which does not contribute to the known physiological roles of its RNA counterpart. RNA-Seq-based transcriptome analyses revealed that multiple aminoglycoside resistance genes, including those of the AmgR regulon, are differentially expressed depending on PhrS-P. AmgR is the response regulator of the AmgRS two-component system (TCS), which affects aminoglycoside and zinc resistance in P. aeruginosa. A PhrS-P-deficient mutant strain exhibited reduced fitness when exposed to sub-inhibitory concentrations of the aminoglycosides tobramycin and amikacin as well as zinc. Based on our findings, we present a working model wherein PhrS-P positively regulates the AmgRS TCS activity through an unknown mechanism, leading to increased bacterial fitness in the presence of aminoglycosides.

title: Comparative transcriptomics reveals a novel variant of an energy signaling regulator for lateral branch domestication in cucumber.
abstract: Genetic alleles derived from wild resources are of great importance for crop breeding and improvement; however, connecting the dots between the functional variants and genetic traits is a significant challenge due to the need for precise, diverse, and large-scale phenotyping. Differential transcripts, which carry genetic variants or alternative splicing (AS) sites, may exhibit altered gene expression and protein coding, therefore influence phenotypes, showing their potential for high-throughput identification of functional genes. In this study, full-length transcripts were assembled and analyzed from eight developmental stage tissues of wild and cultivated cucumbers, utilizing PacBio Iso-seq and Illumina RNA-seq. We identified 6,980 genes underwent AS in cucumber. Approximately 66% of AS events were cultivar-specific, and genetic variants significantly increased around these divergent AS events. Based on the transcript structure of genes and variant annotation, we focused on cis-acting genetic variants that may affect gene function, in which a 21-bp insertion in the 5' untranslated region (UTR) of SnRK-Activating Kinase1 (CsSnAK1), an energy signaling regulator, was demonstrated to inhibit lateral branch development in cultivated cucumber by promoting CsSnAK1 mRNA abundance. Our work provides a straightforward yet reliable approach for integrating transcript structure and variant annotation to identify novel functional alleles in domestication traits.

title: Loss of FCN3 links cirrhotic matrix stiffness to YAP activation in HCC.
abstract: Cirrhosis-associated matrix stiffness is a major biophysical driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). How fibrosis-induced stiffness activates oncogenic YAP signaling remains unclear. We investigated the role of ficolin-3 (FCN3) in stiffness-associated regulation of the O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT)-YAP axis in HCC. Public transcriptomic datasets comparing cirrhotic and normal liver tissues (GSE114564), as well as HCC tissues from patients with and without cirrhosis (GSE14520), were analyzed. FCN3 protein expression was evaluated in 67 paired HCC and adjacent non-tumorous tissues, and a subset of 20 matched cases was further analyzed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR and atomic force microscopy. Controlled-stiffness substrates, FCN3 gain- and loss-of-function models, and murine H22 allograft and human HepG2 xenograft models were used for functional validation. Mechanistic studies included RNA sequencing, cycloheximide chase assays, subcellular fractionation, co-immunoprecipitation, structural prediction, YAP-S127A rescue, Thiamet-G treatment, and YAP knockdown. FCN3 was downregulated in cirrhotic liver and HCC with cirrhosis. In clinical samples, tumor stiffness inversely correlated with FCN3 expression. FCN3 overexpression curtailed proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, and invasion in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Transcriptomics revealed YAP pathway inhibition without changes in upstream kinases. FCN3 did not alter YAP mRNA but reduced YAP protein, increased p-YAP(S127), limited nuclear YAP, and shortened YAP half-life. Co-IP showed FCN3 binds OGT and disrupts OGT-YAP association, decreasing YAP O-GlcNAcylation. YAP knockdown partially attenuated FCN3's anti-tumor effects. These findings support a stiffness-associated FCN3-OGT-YAP regulatory model in HCC, in which FCN3 expression is associated with reduced OGT-YAP interaction, decreased YAP O-GlcNAcylation, and restricted YAP nuclear activity. Further studies are required to establish direct molecular competition and its independence from canonical Hippo-LATS signaling.

title: Fine mapping of yll prioritizes aberrantly spliced Glyma.10G090700 (GmPAO7) as the strongest candidate in a soybean yellow-leaf lethal mutant.
abstract: Chlorophyll-deficient mutants are useful for dissecting chloroplast biology in crops. Here, we characterized a recessive soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) yellow-leaf lethal mutant, yll, that showed markedly reduced chlorophyll content, impaired photosystem II performance, and seedling lethality. Fine mapping delimited yll to a 165-kb interval on chromosome 10. In the Wm82.a6.v1 annotation, this interval contains two genes, of which Glyma.10G090700 (GmPAO7) was prioritized as the strongest candidate on the basis of leaf expression, reduced transcript abundance in yll, and a reproducible intron-retention event. Retention of the 110-bp intron between exons 1 and 2 introduced a premature termination codon and was predicted to shorten the annotated 500-aa PAO1-like protein to 32 aa, eliminating the annotated flavin amine oxidase and NAD(P)-binding domains. Direct sequencing of RT-PCR products detected the normally spliced transcript in wild-type plants and the intron-retained sequence in mutant plants, with overlapping splice forms in heterozygous plants; this qualitative assay does not establish splice-isoform proportions. RNA-seq identified broad expression differences between wild-type and mutant sibling seedlings, including enrichment of photosynthesis-, chloroplast-, and redox-associated categories; because yll seedlings were severely chlorotic and developmentally compromised, these profiles are interpreted as the transcriptomic state associated with the phenotype and may largely reflect downstream responses. Transmission electron microscopy revealed chloroplast ultrastructural abnormalities associated with yll, including poorly developed grana and disorganized thylakoid membranes, but these observations do not functionally validate the candidate gene. Together, the mapping and transcript evidence prioritize Glyma.10G090700 (GmPAO7) as the strongest candidate for yll; Glyma.10G091000 remains in the interval, and functional complementation or an independent allele will be required to establish causality. A PAO-polyamine-ROS connection remains a testable hypothesis because PAO activity, polyamine concentrations, and ROS were not measured.

title: IER3-N-cadherin axis contributes to apoptosis resistance in dermal fibroblasts under profibrotic conditions
abstract: Background: Persistent activation and resistance to apoptosis of dermal fibroblasts contribute to pathological skin fibrosis. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in cell survival, but its role in cutaneous fibrosis remains unclear. We investigated the functional significance of IER3 in dermal fibroblasts and its potential contribution to fibrosis. Methods: IER3 expression was examined in skin samples from patients with systemic sclerosis, keloids, and hypertrophic scars. Primary human dermal fibroblasts were stimulated with transforming growth factor-{beta}1 (TGF-{beta}1). RNA sequencing, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, quantitative PCR, and flow cytometric apoptosis assays were performed to investigate the downstream mechanisms and functional consequences of IER3 expression. Results: IER3 expression was increased in dermal fibroblasts within fibrotic skin lesions and was induced by TGF-{beta}1 independently of SMAD3 and MEK/ERK signaling. Transcriptomic analysis identified CDH2, encoding N-cadherin, as a downstream target of IER3. Moreover, TGF-{beta}1 induced CDH2 expression in a SMAD3 phosphorylation-dependent manner. IER3 knockdown attenuated TGF-{beta}1-induced CDH2 expression, whereas CDH2 knockdown did not affect IER3 expression. Furthermore, CDH2 knockdown enhanced staurosporine-induced apoptosis in TGF-{beta}1-stimulated fibroblasts, accompanied by a shift in apoptosis-related gene expression toward a pro-apoptotic profile. Conclusion: Our findings identify a previously unrecognized IER3-N-cadherin regulatory axis that may promote dermal fibroblast survival by suppressing apoptosis under profibrotic conditions. Targeting this pathway may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for persistent skin fibrosis.

title: Clinicopathologic and molecular features of head and neck NUT carcinoma: Analysis of 25 cases, including 5 with adenoid differentiation.
abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) carcinoma is a highly aggressive malignancy driven by NUTM1 gene fusions, with a median overall survival of 6.5-10.6 months. A comprehensive summary of the morphological and molecular features of head and neck NUT carcinoma is lacking, resulting in inconsistencies in diagnosis and treatment. To characterize the pathological and molecular features of primary head and neck NUT carcinoma and explore optimal management strategies. This study was a single-center retrospective analysis. Fluorescence in situ hybridization was used to detect NUTM1 gene rearrangements. RNA sequencing was performed to analyze the genomic and immune landscapes. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated in relation to patient characteristics and treatment modalities. This study included 25 patients with NUT carcinoma. Adenoid differentiation was observed in 5 cases (2 NSD3 fusions, 1 BRD3 fusion, and 2 BRD4 fusions). Neuroendocrine differentiation was identified in 9 cases (36%). The most common NUT fusion partner was BRD4 (86%), followed by NSD3 (9%) and BRD3 (5%). Tumors with adenoid differentiation showed significant upregulation of COL4A5, H2AFY2, and FLJ00104 and significantly reduced M2 macrophage infiltration (P < 0.05). Compared with the BRD3/BRD4 fusion group, the NSD3 fusion group exhibited 407 downregulated and 14 upregulated genes (FDR < 0.05). Tumors with BRD3/BRD4 fusions had a significantly lower proportion of resting CD4+ memory T cells than those with NSD3 fusions (P < 0.05). The neuroendocrine-positive subgroup showed significant overexpression of PHF21B (P = 0.025). Follow-up data indicated that early radiotherapy significantly reduced mortality (P = 0.017). Patients with neuroendocrine differentiation had significantly higher mortality than those without (P = 0.019). Patients with NUT with adenoid differentiation or different gene fusions exhibit distinct gene expression profiles and immune landscapes. Neuroendocrine differentiation is associated with poor prognosis. Radiotherapy may be associated with favourable outcomes and warrants further investigation.

title: Long non-coding RNA RP3-380B8.4 facilitates tumor malignancy, liver metastasis and shapes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) participate in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and immune regulation. However, the biological functions of lncRNA RP3-380B8.4 (RP3) in CRC and its relationship with the tumor immune microenvironment remain unclear. RP3 expression in CRC was assessed using public datasets and validated by in situ hybridization (ISH). We further examined the expression levels and intracellular localization of RP3 in CRC cells by qRT-PCR. The effect of RP3 on the cell growth, migration, invasion and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) was investigated by in vitro experiments and western blot. In vivo experiments confirmed that RP3 potentiated tumor growth and liver metastasis in CRC. We predicted the mechanism by RNA-seq, and confirmed them by western blot. The impact of RP3 on the tumor immune microenvironment was analyzed by bioinformatics analysis and flow cytometry. RP3 was substantially elevated in CRC tissues and associated with poor prognosis. RP3 overexpression increased CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT in vitro. RP3 overexpression accelerated orthotopic colorectal cancer growth and liver metastasis in nude mice. On the contrary, knockdown of RP3 achieved the opposite effect. Mechanistically, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and western blot analysis revealed that RP3 overexpression is associated with enrichment of MYC target gene programs and elevated c-Myc protein levels in colorectal cancer. Furthermore, overexpression of RP3 significantly reduced the infiltration of CD8+ T cells in the tumor, while inhibiting the polarization of macrophages toward the CD86-positive (M1-like) phenotype. Conversely, knockdown of RP3 effectively ameliorated this tumor immunosuppressive microenvironment. RP3 facilitates CRC proliferation and metastasis and exerts immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. These findings implicate RP3 as a candidate regulator in CRC whose mechanistic and therapeutic potential requires further validation.

title: Spatial architecture of the synovium identifies clinically relevant phenotypes of osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous joint disease characterized by marked variability in etiology and clinical symptoms. We aimed to determine whether spatial organization of synovial tissue underlies clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA. We developed a deep learning-based semantic segmentation framework to analyze hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images of human synovium. Spatial entropy and inter-tissue connectivity metrics were incorporated to evaluate local pathology. We further applied graph neural network-based community modeling to classify tissue structures based on their microenvironment. The model identified key OA-associated histological features, including synovial lining hyperplasia, immune cell infiltration, angiogenesis, and fibrotic remodeling. Quantitative analysis of tissue composition revealed that enrichment of dense fibrous tissue was associated with poorer postoperative outcomes. However, tissue proportion alone did not adequately capture baseline disease status. Inter-tissue connectivity-based analysis showed that enrichment of Lining-Micro vessel interactions was associated with lower preoperative KOOS Symptom scores, indicating more severe symptoms, and elevated synovitis scores. Using features derived from graph neural network-based modeling, Micro vessels segregated into two distinct communities, one enriched in adjacent lining structures and another associated with immune-rich regions, and their relative abundances varied among knee OA patients. Integration with matched synovial single-cell RNA sequencing data showed increased predicted interactions between lining fibroblasts and endothelial cells in the Lining-Micro vessel-rich phenotype. These interactions were enriched for angiogenesis-related VEGF and ANGPTL signaling, providing supportive evidence for a distinct fibroblast-endothelial signaling state. These findings indicate that the spatial organization of synovial architecture, beyond simple tissue composition, captures clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA and links histological microenvironments to cell-cell communication networks.

title: CKAP4 silencing impairs growth and survival of esophageal adenocarcinoma cells in vitro.
abstract: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) is the predominant histologic subtype of esophageal cancer in Western countries and has a poor prognosis. Cytoskeleton-associated protein 4 (CKAP4), a transmembrane receptor involved in proliferation, migration, and signaling, has been implicated in several cancers, but its role in EAC remains unclear. We investigated CKAP4 expression and cellular changes associated with CKAP4 depletion in EAC cell models. CKAP4 expression was characterized using an in vitro Barrett's esophagus (BE) model of EAC progression. CKAP4 was silenced by siRNA in OE33 and OE19 EAC cells. Functional and molecular effects were assessed, and transcriptional changes were analyzed by RNA sequencing. CKAP4 expression varied across Barrett's neoplastic progression, with highest total expression in dysplastic cells and marked surface overexpression in OE33, OE19, and FLO-1 EAC cells. CKAP4 depletion reduced CKAP4 mRNA and protein, altered cell morphology, decreased viability and proliferation, and increased apoptosis. AKT phosphorylation was reduced in OE19 cells and MAPK phosphorylation in OE33 cells, whereas ß-catenin and GSK3ß activity remained unchanged. CKAP4 silencing increased surface expression of adhesion molecules, including integrins α5/ß1 in OE33 cells. RNA sequencing identified >500 differentially expressed genes enriched in immune-related pathways, indicating immune-related transcriptional changes. CKAP4 is a functionally relevant, surface-overexpressed protein in Barrett's-associated EAC. These findings define cellular and transcriptional changes associated with CKAP4 depletion in EAC cells in vitro and support further mechanistic and preclinical investigation; therapeutic and biomarker relevance in EAC remains to be established.

title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanisms of Yinxieping Tablets in Psoriasis Treatment Based on Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Experimental Validation.
abstract: Psoriasis is a prevalent immune-mediated chronic inflammatory skin disease, with a pathology defined by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and immune cell infiltration. Yinxieping Tablets (YXPT), a traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting solely of rosin, have been clinically used to alleviate psoriatic symptoms. However, their underlying mechanisms of action remain to be fully elucidated. We established an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and systematically screened the potential targets and pathways of YXPT using integrated network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning, transcriptome sequencing, and molecular docking. Key findings were experimentally validated by Western blot and qPCR in a psoriasis-like mouse model. YXPT treatment improved psoriasiform skin lesions and was associated with lower lesional Ki67 expression and serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels; high-dose YXPT also reduced the spleen index. Integrated analyses identified six candidate genes (BCL2, LYN, SYK, CCR2, AURKA, and ADRB2), with CCR2 emerging as the sole overlap with RNA-seq-derived genes. CCR2-based gene-set analysis showed enrichment of PI3K/Akt- and NF-κB-related pathways. Following YXPT treatment, lesional CCR2 protein and mRNA levels, phosphorylation of PI3K, Akt, p38, and p65, and mRNA levels of PI3K, Akt, p38, ERK1/2, and p65 were lower than in the IMQ group. YXPT ameliorated psoriasis-like skin lesions in the IMQ mouse model, accompanied by lower CCR2 expression and changes in PI3K/Akt, MAPK, and NF-κB pathway components. These findings nominate CCR2 as a candidate for further study, while its causal role and relationship to the signaling changes remain to be established.

title: Pinin Modulation Restores Chemosensitivity in SW620 and HCT-116 Colon Cancer Cells.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to the emergence of resistance to standard chemotherapeutic regimens. The identification of molecular determinants of chemoresistance is therefore critical to improve patient stratification and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we investigate the functional role of Pinin (PNN), a multifunctional protein involved in RNA processing and gene regulation, in mediating chemoresistance in CRC. SW620 and HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells were used to investigate the functional role of PNN. Pnn expression was silenced by siRNA and lentiviral shRNA approaches. Cell sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil and oxaliplatin was evaluated by MTT assay, while apoptosis was assessed by Annexin V/7-AAD flow cytometry. Migration, invasion, and clonogenic capacity were analyzed using wound-healing, modified Boyden chamber, and colony formation assays. Metabolic reprogramming following Pnn depletion was characterized using Seahorse extracellular flux analysis. Transcriptomic alterations were investigated by Nanopore RNA sequencing, followed by differential gene expression, bioinformatic, and gene set enrichment analyses. Pnn silencing significantly enhanced sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil and oxaliplatin in SW620 cells, as demonstrated by reduced cell viability, decreased IC50 values, and increased apoptotic responses. Transcriptomic profiling revealed extensive gene expression reprogramming, affecting pathways related to cell cycle progression, DNA damage response, and stress signaling. To corroborate these findings, Pnn-silenced HCT-116 cells were used to confirm the observed cytotoxic effects and independently validate selected differentially expressed genes identified by RNA-seq in SW620 cells. Notably, Pnn depletion induced a marked impairment of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation without compensatory glycolytic activation, indicating reduced metabolic flexibility under stress conditions. Functionally, Pnn silencing also decreased clonogenic capacity and invasive behavior. Collectively, these findings identify Pnn as a key regulator of chemoresistance and reveal its involvement in transcriptional control, metabolic adaptation, and stress response. Targeting PNN-related pathways may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to restore chemosensitivity and improve outcomes in colorectal cancer, although further validation is required.

title: Platelet and megakaryocyte function in the pathogenesis of POEMS syndrome.
abstract: Polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal protein, and skin changes (POEMS) syndrome is a rare plasma cell dyscrasia characterized by multisystem manifestations and markedly elevated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) levels, identified as a sensitive biomarker for disease progression. Serum VEGF exceeds plasma levels, implicating platelets as a potential reservoir of VEGF in POEMS syndrome. However, the precise cellular origin of VEGF and the underlying pathological mechanisms remain elusive and challenging to elucidate. We conducted the first comprehensive multi-omics analysis of platelets from patients with POEMS syndrome, integrating RNA sequencing and quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics. RNA sequencing revealed a distinct platelet transcriptome enriched for platelet activation-related genes. Flow cytometry and electron microscopy confirmed a highly activated platelet status. Mass spectrometry revealed an altered platelet proteome with upregulated protein synthesis and abundant ribosomes, indicating enhanced protein synthesis pathway in POEMS syndrome. Importantly, we demonstrated that the megakaryocyte-platelet axis, rather than plasma cells, is the primary source of excess VEGF. Platelet VEGF levels were significantly higher in patients than in healthy donors (P < 0.0001). VEGFA mRNA in situ hybridization confirmed significantly increased VEGFA expression in bone marrow megakaryocytes from patients (P < 0.01). These findings redefine the cellular origin of VEGF in POEMS syndrome and highlight the role of the megakaryocyte-platelet axis in the disease biology. Our study provides critical mechanistic insights into a long-standing mystery of this disorder, underscoring the need to further elucidate its functional interplay with clonal plasma cells.

title: S100A9 Mediates Neuroblastoma-Associated Skeletal Muscle Atrophy via O-GlcNAcylation Repression and Activate Mitophagy Activation.
abstract: In patients with neuroblastoma (NB), skeletal muscle atrophy is a key factor linked to poor survival and decreased long-term quality of life. Nevertheless, there are still insufficient therapeutic methods that work, and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. As persistent inflammation is a hallmark of tumour-related muscle atrophy, this study aims to identify the key inflammatory mediators causing NB-related muscle atrophy and systematically elucidate the downstream molecular mechanism. The adverse biological features of NB were used to identify potential inflammatory mediators causing muscle atrophy. Serum samples from NB patients and NB mouse models were then used to confirm the clinical relevance of these candidates to skeletal muscle atrophy. Recombinant inflammatory proteins and certain inhibitors were given in vivo to define the functional impact of mediators. Additionally, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) and Western blotting were used to methodically examine the underlying molecular pathways of NB-induced muscle atrophy. Both NB patients with muscle atrophy and NB mouse models had considerably higher serum levels of the pro-inflammatory mediator S100A9 protein (p < 0.001). Recombinant mouse S100A9 protein functionally reduced skeletal muscle weight and upregulated the atrophy markers TRIM63/FBXO32 in mice (p < 0.05), whereas its inhibitor, ABR-238901, successfully reduced muscle atrophy and downregulated these atrophy markers in the NB model (p < 0.001). Mechanistically, S100A9 inhibited skeletal muscle protein O-GlcNAcylation via its receptor RAGE (p < 0.05). Muscle atrophy was ultimately caused by the abnormal activation of BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy that resulted from this suppression. Lastly, by inhibiting this mitophagy route, in vivo administration of the O-GlcNAcylation agonist Thiamet G considerably reduced skeletal muscle atrophy in NB mice (p < 0.05). Our study identifies S100A9 as a critical mediator of NB-associated skeletal muscle atrophy through a novel RAGE/O-GlcNAcylation/mitophagy axis, establishing S100A9 as a potential therapeutic target and providing a rationale for early interventional strategies to preserve muscle mass and improve patient outcomes.

title: NEDD9 confers ferroptosis resistance in liver cancer by inhibiting autophagy via the AKT‑mTOR signaling pathway.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most prevalent primary liver malignancy, is characterized by poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Ferroptosis, a recently identified form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy. Neural precursor cell expressed, developmentally downregulated 9 (NEDD9) is a scaffold protein implicated in tumor progression; however, its role in the regulation of ferroptosis remains unclear. NEDD9 was overexpressed or knocked down in liver cancer cells using lentiviral vectors. RNA sequencing was performed to analyze transcriptomic changes. Cell viability and death were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and propidium iodide (PI) staining assays. C11-BODIPY 581/591, malondialdehyde (MDA), Western blot, dihydroethidium (DHE) and iron assays were used to detect lipid peroxidation, MDA content, protein expression, reactive oxygen species (ROS) and Fe²⁺ levels, respectively. Autophagy was modulated using Torin1 (activator) and chloroquine (inhibitor). For in vivo experiments, NEDD9‑knockdown Hepa1‑6 cells were subcutaneously injected into C57BL/6 mice to assess tumor growth and ferroptosis‑related sensitivity to sorafenib. RSL3- and sorafenib-induced ferroptosis in HCC cells was accompanied by a significant reduction in NEDD9 expression. NEDD9 overexpression upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and conferred resistance to ferroptosis, whereas NEDD9 knockdown decreased GPX4 expression, elevated ROS and MDA levels, and markedly sensitized cells to ferroptosis. Mechanistically, our findings support a model in which NEDD9-associated AKT-mTOR signaling contributes to ferroptosis resistance through the regulation of autophagy-related processes. More specifically, NEDD9 overexpression activated AKT-mTOR signaling and suppressed autophagy, thereby maintaining GPX4 abundance without altering intracellular Fe²⁺ levels, whereas autophagy activation attenuated NEDD9-mediated ferroptosis resistance. In contrast, NEDD9 knockdown attenuated AKT-mTOR signaling and was associated with lysosome-dependent GPX4 loss and intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy reversed the ferroptosis-promoting effect caused by NEDD9 knockdown. In vivo, NEDD9 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and potentiated the antitumor efficacy of the ferroptosis‑inducing agent sorafenib. Ferroptosis in HCC cells was accompanied by decreased NEDD9 expression. NEDD9 overexpression markedly inhibited ferroptosis, whereas NEDD9 knockdown promoted it. These findings suggest that targeting NEDD9 may represent a potential strategy for enhancing the therapeutic response to ferroptosis-associated treatments in liver cancer.

title: Single-cell atlas of the developing mouse oviduct reveals smooth muscle heterogeneity and identifies Vps34 as a critical regulator of female fertility.
abstract: The oviduct smooth muscle layer is traditionally regarded as a contractile unit. Limited understanding exists regarding the molecular heterogeneity and intercellular communication during development timeline, which is critical for female reproductive function. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to profile the cellular composition of mice oviducts at four developmental stages: neonatal (7 days), pre-pubertal (3 weeks), young adult (8 weeks) and middle-aged (9 months). We aim to provide a framework for further investigation of oviduct biology and associated reproductive disorders. We delineate three distinct (SMC) subtypes, with their relative proportions shifting dynamically across the developmental timeline. SMC1 represented a transient progenitor population exclusive to neonatal oviducts. SMC2 displayed a mature contractile phenotype, while SMC3 uniquely expressed hormone-responsive genes (Esr1, Pgr) and showed enrichment of autophagy-related pathways. Functional studies demonstrated that SMC-specific deletion of Vps34 disrupts oviduct coiling and muscular integrity, leading to vacuolar degeneration and a significant reduction in litter size in mice. Additionally, we map five ciliated and six secretory epithelial subtypes and suggest that FN1 signaling may serve as a potential mediator of crosstalk between epithelial and SMCs during development, with the FN1-SDC4 axis emerging as the dominant interaction in mature oviducts. Thus, while the contractile and hormone-responsive functions of the oviductal muscle layer have long been recognized, our work provides its underlying cellular complexity during development. Our study constructs a developmental atlas of murine oviduct SMCs, revealing that the myosalpinx is composed of functionally distinct SMC subtypes with dynamic developmental trajectories. The identification of Vps34 as a critical guardian of myosalpinx integrity offers a new cellular framework for understanding human tubal pathologies. These findings highlight the importance of SMC subtype homeostasis and autophagy-mediated maintenance of myosalpinx structure, providing a basis for future mechanistic studies on oviduct function and dysfunction.

title: Postoperative inulin supplementation is associated with microbiota remodeling and improved colonic anastomotic healing in LPS-primed mice.
abstract: Anastomotic leakage is a major colorectal surgical complication that may be exacerbated by perioperative inflammatory stress. How transcriptomic profiles and tissue-adherent microbiota change under such stress, and whether postoperative inulin supplementation is associated with microbiota changes and improved healing after inflammatory priming, remain unclear. Two independent animal experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared control (CON) and LPS-primed mice using scheduled, repeated-cross-sectional sampling for microbiota profiling on POD0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 14 and for RNA-seq on POD0, 1, 3, 5, and 7. Experiment 2 used the same murine colonic anastomosis model to evaluate postoperative exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) with or without inulin supplementation (dietary fiber, DF) in a 2 × 2 factorial design comprising CON, CON-DF, LPS, and LPS-DF groups. Healing was assessed by survival, recovery scores, anastomotic burst pressure, histology, immunostaining, and short-chain-fatty-acid quantification. Within Experiment 2, a dedicated n = 10/group survival/longitudinal cohort was followed through POD5, and a separate terminal cohort provided six surviving mice/group for POD5 assessments; five microscopy fields were averaged within each mouse. LPS priming impaired healing and induced niche-specific microbiota alterations with altered bacterial microspatial patterns at the suture line. DF supplementation was associated with improved recovery and anastomotic strength, reduced inflammatory infiltration, increased proliferation, decreased apoptosis, and altered inflammatory- and repair-associated immune markers. The planned LPS-DF versus LPS survival comparison in the POD5 four-group cohort was not significant after multiplicity correction. At POD5, DF was associated with lower Shannon diversity and an altered short-chain-fatty-acid profile, including higher acetate; the LPS × inulin interactions for these measures were not significant. Brief postoperative inulin-supplemented EEN improved anastomotic healing following inflammatory priming, concurrent with microbiota remodeling and short-chain-fatty-acid differences, including higher acetate. These concurrent changes do not establish microbiota- or SCFA-mediated causality.

title: Transcriptional signatures associated with environmental and developmental variation in tobacco aroma-related pathways across cultivars and regions.
abstract: Tobacco aroma is a complex quality trait shaped by interactions among genotype, developmental progression, and regional environment, yet the transcriptional programs linking ecological context to aroma-related metabolism remain incompletely understood. We profiled the transcriptomes of ten Nicotiana tabacum L. cultivars grown in three representative regions and sampled at three developmental stages. Normalized RNA-seq expression, principal component analysis, differential expression analysis, soft clustering, pathway enrichment, gene-expression variability analysis, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were performed. Growing region was the major source of transcriptomic variation, followed by developmental stage, whereas cultivar effects were comparatively smaller. Leaf maturation from S1 to S3 was associated with repression of photosynthesis and carbon-assimilation pathways and induction of stress responses, redox regulation, cell-wall and membrane remodeling, amino acid metabolism, and secondary metabolism. Aroma-associated processes, including carotenoid-, phenylpropanoid-, and redox-related pathways, showed regiondependent expression patterns. Strong-aroma cultivars exhibited greater transcriptional variability across regions than light-aroma cultivars, suggesting stronger environmental responsiveness of their regulatory networks. Network analysis further highlighted candidate hub genes, including the heat shockrelated protein A0A1S4A548 and peroxiredoxin Q A0A1S4B900, in temperature- and oxidative-stress-related modules. These findings provide a transcriptome-level framework for understanding how environmental context and developmental maturation are associated with aroma-related metabolic reprogramming in tobacco and identify candidate genes for future functional validation.

title: Antigen-driven CD8+ T cell activation drives the immunopathogenesis of myasthenia gravis-associated myocarditis.
abstract: Myasthenia gravis-associated myocarditis (MG-myocarditis) is a life-threatening condition. However, the immune dysregulation underlying its pathogenesis remains poorly defined. This study aimed to delineate the immunological pathways driving myocarditis development in patients with MG. We performed integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and paired T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire profiling on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 3 patients with MG-myocarditis and 4 patients with MG-only. Analyses were conducted to characterize transcriptional states, differentiation trajectories, clonal expansions, and antigen-specific signatures associated with MG-myocarditis. Although the overall proportions of major PBMC lineages did not differ significantly between groups, transcriptomic profiling revealed substantial numbers of significantly differentially expressed genes across multiple immune cell subsets. Classical CD14+ monocytes displayed a marked skewing toward a pro-inflammatory differentiation trajectory, accompanied by downregulation of the Activator Protein-1-high intermediate state associated with anti-inflammatory programming. Within the T cell compartment, MG-myocarditis was characterized by robust expansion of TCR clonotypes concurrently enriched in CD8+ effector memory with high EOMES expression and CD8+ effector subsets, indicative of recent or ongoing antigen-driven activation.TCR-peptide binding prediction analysis showed preferential reactivity of these expanded clonotypes toward cardiac proteins-including Titin, MYO10, and MYH6-implicating antigen-specific cytotoxicity in myocardial injury. In parallel, non-classical CD16+ monocytes and conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) exhibited enhanced antigen-presenting signatures, marked respectively by S100A8 upregulation and LY6E downregulation. Our findings identify non-classical CD16+ monocytes and cDCs as potential cardiac antigen-presenting populations capable of priming pathogenic CD8+ T cell responses, thereby contributing to the immunopathogenesis of MG-associated myocarditis.

title: Immune-intrinsic MLKL regulates dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell effector function in anti-tumor immunity.
abstract: Anti-tumor immunity relies on coordinated interactions between dendritic cells (DCs) and cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells to eliminate malignant cells. Mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL), a key executioner of necroptosis, has recently been implicated in cancer through necroptosis-independent functions and is being explored as a therapeutic target. However, most studies have focused on tumor cells, whereas the immune-intrinsic functions of MLKL remain poorly understood. In particular, MLKL expression across immune cell subsets and its role in anti-tumor immunity have not been systematically investigated. Transcriptomic analyses revealed broad MLKL expression across multiple immune cell subsets, including neutrophils, monocytes, dendritic cells, and activated/memory Tcell subsets. Consistent with these findings, MLKL was upregulated in primary mouse immune cells following activation, including Tcell stimulation, bone marrow-derived dendritic cell (BMDC) maturation, and M1 macrophages. Pharmacological inhibition of MLKL impaired BMDC maturation, reduced DC-mediated CD8⁺ T cell priming, and suppressed CD8⁺ T cell activation, proliferation, and cytotoxic killing of B16-OVA tumor cells. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing analyses from cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) further showed that MLKL expression was enriched in activated and effector CD8⁺ T cell subsets. Donor-level analyses showed higher MLKL expression in T cells from ICB responders than in those from non-responders, particularly in post-treatment samples. These findings associate MLKL expression with activated and effector anti-tumor Tcell states and suggest its potential relevance to ICB response. Collectively, these findings show that MLKL is upregulated during immune activation and contributes to DC maturation and CD8⁺ T cell effector responses. Our findings highlight the context-dependent roles of MLKL across tumor and immune compartments and emphasize the importance of considering immune-intrinsic MLKL functions in the development of MLKL-targeted therapies for precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas of Kidney-Yang and Kidney-Yin deficiency syndromes reveals distinct osteoimmune-stromal programs underlying osteopenia and osteoporosis.
abstract: Osteopenia and osteoporosis are escalating health burdens lacking precise therapeutic strategies owing to pronounced disease heterogeneity. Kidney-Yang deficiency (KYangD, "cold syndrome") and Kidney-Yin deficiency (KYinD, "heat syndrome") represent two major traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-defined syndromes underlying these conditions, but their molecular basis remains obscure. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on bone tissue from osteopenia/osteoporosis patients stratified by KYangD, KYinD, or non-deficiency group, generating the first transcriptomic atlas of syndrome-specific osteoimmune and stromal programs. KYangD exhibited an energy- and perfusion-limited, low-grade inflammation in type H-like capillary endothelial cells (CD31highEMCNhigh). This inflammation was characterized by incomplete angiogenic activation, reduced phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-protein kinase B (AKT)/hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1)/nitric oxide (NO) signaling despite compensatory Notch signaling, and weakened extracellular matrix/adhesion that restricts osteoblast maturation. KYinD was dominated by inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress with nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)/tumor necrosis factor (TNF)/interleukin (IL)-17 activation, protease-rich matrix remodeling, and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1)-mediated adhesion, alongside broad attenuation of Notch signaling, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), angiopoietin 1 (ANGPT1), and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (CXCL12) scaffolds and loss of bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β), and Wnt osteogenic pathways. These alterations spanned endothelial, stromal, osteolineage, and immune compartments with network-level rewiring of intercellular communication. Collectively, our findings establish the first single-cell molecular bridge between TCM-defined syndromes and osteoporotic pathology, providing a framework for syndrome-specific precision interventions, namely, restoring energy metabolism and vascular-osteogenic coupling in KYangD, and suppressing hyper-inflammation while rebuilding endothelial scaffolds in KYinD.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis identifies a manganese-associated transcriptional signature and a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature in COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling.
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous respiratory disease involving airway inflammation, emphysema, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manganese exposure has been linked to pulmonary inflammation and oxidative stress, but its molecular association with COPD vascular pathology remains unclear. This study explored a manganese-associated transcriptional signature in COPD and investigated its potential relationship with endothelial cell dysfunction and vascular remodeling. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were used to calculate a manganese-related transcriptional score, identify differentially expressed genes, and characterize WGCNA modules. Manganese-COPD-associated genes were obtained by intersecting manganese-related genes, COPD differentially expressed genes, and manganese-associated module genes. Functional enrichment, PPI analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, diagnostic modeling, and consensus clustering were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed to characterize HBEGF expression, endothelial subpopulations, CytoTRACE2 scores, pseudotime dynamics, transcription factor activity, cell-cell communication, and NicheNet ligand-target relationships. COPD samples showed significantly higher manganese-related transcriptional scores. A total of 43 manganese-COPD-associated candidate genes were identified and were enriched mainly in pathways related to inflammation, cytokines, immune chemotaxis, and vascular processes. Machine learning identified 14 core diagnostic genes, and the combined model showed good classification performance in the training and validation cohorts. Among these genes, HBEGF showed the highest contribution in the ElasticNet model and was prioritized for downstream analysis. Consensus clustering divided COPD samples into two molecular subtypes with distinct manganese-related scores and functional features. Single-cell analysis suggested that HBEGF was closely associated with endothelial cell alterations, especially venous endothelial cells. Pseudotime and transcription factor analyses suggested a potential JUN/HBEGF regulatory relationship. CellChat and NicheNet analyses further indicated that venous endothelial cell-derived HBEGF may participate in endothelial-smooth muscle cell communication. This study identified an elevated manganese-related transcriptional score in COPD and prioritized HBEGF as a key candidate associated with venous endothelial cell state changes and endothelial-smooth muscle communication. These findings suggest a potential JUN/HBEGF-associated endothelial signature relevant to COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling, which warrants further experimental validation.

title: Integrated Computational Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Identify the PLK2-TFEB Axis as a Therapeutic Mechanism of Kunkui Baoshen Decoction in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Metabolic stress and lipid homeostasis imbalance in proximal tubular cells (PTC) are increasingly recognized as critical contributors to diabetic kidney disease (DKD) progression, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Kunkui Baoshen Decoction (KKBS) has shown clinical benefits in DKD, but its molecular basis remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the therapeutic targets and regulatory mechanisms of KKBS in DKD-associated proximal tubular injury. An integrated multi-omics strategy combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, machine learning, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was applied to identify candidate therapeutic targets of KKBS in DKD. Then, the protective effects of KKBS were further evaluated in db/db mice and high-glucose and high-lipid (HGHL)-induced HK-2 cells by assessing renal function, lipid metabolism, autophagic flux, transcription factor EB (TFEB) nuclear translocation, and fibrosis-related markers. KKBS effectively reduced urinary protein excretion, corrected aberrant lipid metabolism, and mitigated renal fibrotic lesions in db/db mice. Integrated multi-omics profiling highlighted polo-like kinase 2 (PLK2) as a potential therapeutic target, and scRNA-seq analysis demonstrated its progressive upregulation in PTC during DKD progression. Mechanistically, KKBS treatment reduced PLK2 expression, restored TFEB nuclear translocation, improved autophagic flux, and decreased lipid droplet accumulation. Similar effects were reproduced by PLK2 inhibition in HGHL-induced HK-2 cells. These findings support the PLK2-TFEB axis as a potential therapeutic target in DKD. KKBS may alleviate lipid accumulation and fibrotic alterations in DKD by suppressing PLK2 expression, facilitating TFEB nuclear translocation, and restoring autophagy-lysosome-related function.

title: Treg and immune proliferative programs characterize anti-PD-1-responsive endometrial cancer: an integrative single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and TCGA-UCEC reanalysis.
abstract: The responses to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-based therapy in advanced endometrial cancer are heterogeneous. The cellular programs associated with such responses remain incompletely defined, particularly when the immune cell composition, spatial expression patterns, and population-level transcriptomic features are considered together. Publicly available TCGA-UCEC and GSE251923 data were reanalyzed using bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the Visium expression space platform. The GSE251923 dataset included one anti-PD-1 responder and one non-responder; hence, all comparisons between these two cases are descriptive. Prespecified immune- and proliferation-related signatures were evaluated across the datasets, and the Visium clusters were assigned broad marker-based expression compartments. Exploratory quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) assays were used to examine selected transcripts in the Ishikawa and HEC-1A endometrial cancer cell lines under 1% O2 hypoxia and in primary neutrophils exposed to endometrial-cancer ascites-conditioned medium. These assays were used as ancillary models of condition-associated transcription; neither hypoxia nor ascites exposure was treated as a direct model of clinical immune checkpoint inhibitor response. After quality control, we obtained 16,725 single cells that were assigned to 14 populations. Compared with the non-responder sample, the responder sample contained higher proportions of CD8 T cells [+3.1 percentage points (pp)], regulatory T cells (Tregs; +3.3 pp), B cells (+6.7 pp), plasma cells (+5.4 pp), CD4 T cells (+5.9 pp), and proliferating cells (+7.7 pp); the non-responder sample dominantly contained epithelial/tumor and endothelial cells. In TCGA-UCEC (553 tumors and 35 normal tissues), a high Treg signature was associated with longer overall survival [log-rank p = 0.047; hazard ratio (HR) = 0.58; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.34-1.00], whereas a high proliferation signature was associated with shorter overall survival (HR = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.01-2.94; p = 0.046). The responder Visium section showed descriptively higher Treg and proliferation scores with lower epithelial and extracellular matrix scores. Under hypoxia, the two endometrial cancer cell lines showed higher MKI67, FOXP3, CXCL13, PDCD1, and CTLA4 transcript levels; the ascites-conditioned medium increased PAD4 and ELANE expressions in primary neutrophils. The integrated analyses helped identify Treg- and proliferation-related patterns that differed between two anti-PD-1-treated endometrial cancers and were directionally contextualized in TCGA-UCEC. The qRT-PCR assays provide ancillary evidence of condition-associated transcriptional changes but do not validate immune cell states, clinical response mechanisms, or functional neutrophil extracellular trap formation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in independent treatment-annotated cohorts.

title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Identify NFKBIE as a Candidate Gene Associated with IS-II Neutrophil Differentiation in Lung Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
abstract: People undergoing lung transplantation may develop lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), in which neutrophils contribute to the inflammatory response. However, the molecular features associated with distinct neutrophil states remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate molecular features associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil state, with particular attention to NFKBIE, an NF-κB inhibitor. We integrated bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Candidate genes were identified using co-expression analysis and machine-learning methods. We further examined cell-cell communication and the association of NFKBIE with neutrophil states using pseudotime analysis and computational gene perturbation. We validated NFKBIE expression in a mouse model of LIRI using RT-qPCR and Western blotting and assessed lung injury by histological examination. A total of 553 differentially expressed genes and a key disease-associated module containing 4,456 genes were identified, with predominant enrichment in inflammation- and immunity-related pathways (eg, TNF and NF-κB). Five overlapping candidate transcriptomic markers, CXCL3, CYLD, NFKBIE, SLC30A1, and KBTBD8, were identified. The five-gene model showed strong discrimination in the discovery cohort (AUC = 0.986) and also showed strong discrimination in the separate GSE127003 validation dataset (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.996-1.000). Single-cell analysis showed that neutrophils were the largest annotated cell population in both CIT and post-reperfusion samples, whereas the IS-II neutrophil subtype was markedly enriched after reperfusion; NFKBIE was most highly expressed in IS-II neutrophils. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further indicated that elevated NFKBIE expression was associated with a later differentiation state toward the IS-II phenotype, while computational NFKBIE perturbation predicted alterations in several perturbation-associated genes. In vivo validation confirmed that both NFKBIE mRNA and protein levels were upregulated in lung tissue after reperfusion. The five-gene transcriptomic model showed reproducible discriminatory performance in a separate validation dataset. NFKBIE was consistently associated with the IS-II neutrophil state across multiple computational analyses, while in vivo experiments confirmed its increased expression after reperfusion. These findings nominate NFKBIE as a candidate gene associated with IS-II neutrophil differentiation and provide a hypothesis-generating basis for further functional investigation.

title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiling reveals coagulation-associated heterogeneity and prognostic SPINT2 in acute myeloid leukemia.
abstract: Coagulation-associated genes (CARGs) have been implicated in tumor progression and immune regulation, but their cellular heterogeneity and prognostic relevance in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remain incompletely understood. Here, we sought to characterize the cellular and molecular landscape of CARGs in AML and to identify CARG-associated prognostic determinants with potential functional relevance. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were first analyzed to characterize CARG activity across distinct cellular populations in AML. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were subsequently integrated to identify CARG-related molecular subtypes and establish a prognostic scoring system using machine-learning approaches. The associations of the CARG prognostic score with biological pathways, immune characteristics, and drug sensitivity were further evaluated. Single-cell expression patterns, cell-cell communication, and computational perturbation analyses were used to investigate key prognostic genes, followed by experimental validation in AML cells. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed marked heterogeneity of CARG activity across AML cell populations, with particularly high activity observed in erythroid and cycling erythroid populations. Building on these cellular-level observations, bulk transcriptomic analysis identified three distinct CARG-related molecular subtypes with significantly different survival outcomes and biological characteristics. An integrated machine-learning framework established a seven-gene CARG prognostic score that showed prognostic stratification in both the development and independent external validation cohorts. High CARG prognostic scores were associated with distinct metabolic and immune-related transcriptional programs and differential ex vivo responses to several therapeutic agents. Among the model features, SPINT2 showed prominent prognostic importance and displayed cell-type-specific expression at single-cell resolution. Single-cell analysis revealed cell-type-specific SPINT2 expression, while computational perturbation analyses suggested associations with erythroid/heme-related and oxidative metabolic programs. Functional experiments further demonstrated that SPINT2 silencing suppressed AML cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis. Our study defines a cellular and molecular landscape of CARG heterogeneity in AML and establishes an integrated CARG-based framework for prognostic stratification. The combination of single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses, computational perturbation, and functional validation supports SPINT2 as a candidate gene with functional relevance to AML cell growth and survival and provides a basis for further investigation of coagulation-associated biology in AML.

title: Genetically supported protein signals and ferroptosis-related cell states in human intervertebral disc degeneration: local pQTL-FinnGen screening integrated with nucleus pulposus single-cell RNA sequencing.
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) involves nucleus pulposus (NP) cell dysfunction, inflammatory remodeling, and oxidative stress. Genetic support for circulating protein signals and their cell-type-specific context remains incompletely defined. We integrated deCODE cis-pQTL data with FinnGen R12 M13_INTERVERTEB and human NP scRNA-seq (GSE153066). Local MR screening used harmonized variants with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. The scRNA-seq analysis retained 70,622 cells from 16 libraries and used library-level pseudobulk comparisons. A qPCR validation experiment in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells (ATCC TIB-202) evaluated MST1, SAA1, BPI, and GCLM under an inflammatory condition. Four multi-SNP signals passed correction: MST1 showed higher endpoint odds (OR = 1.057, q = 4.15 × 10-6), whereas DLK1 (OR = 0.933, q = 0.016), ITIH1 (OR = 0.926, q = 0.016), and SAA1 (OR = 0.927, q = 0.023) showed inverse associations. TP53I3 and BPI remained nominal exploratory signals. TFRC showed a BH-positive single-SNP result (OR = 1.471, q = 0.023). ScRNA-seq resolved eight broad cell populations and demonstrated between-library heterogeneity; nominal macrophage-composition and selected expression differences did not survive within-panel correction. In the qPCR experiment, relative expression was 1.34 for MST1, 0.31 for SAA1, 3.46 for BPI, and 1.70 for GCLM (control = 1.0; n = 4 independent biological replicates/group; all Welch P < 0.001), consistent with the scRNA-seq directions. The study identifies genetically supported protein signals and ferroptosis-related cellular expression patterns while separating genetic screening from transcriptomic localization. The qPCR experiment provides orthogonal experimental support for selected candidate expression changes in the THP-1 inflammatory model.

title: CXCL12: a key gene in IPF-COPD pathogenesis and its therapeutic potential.
abstract: Shared core genes and molecular mechanisms relevant to the pathological overlap between idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were investigated to inform future diagnostic and therapeutic research. Gene expression profiles were analysed using differential expression gene (DEG) analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. A random forest (RF) model incorporating a multi-feature selection mechanism was used to identify core genes in IPF patients with COPD. The expression levels, diagnostic performance, and immune cell relationships of these genes were analysed, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to assess the expression patterns of the core genes. Finally, drug predictions were made based on the core genes. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were further performed to evaluate candidate CXCL12-ligand interactions, and CXCL12 expression was experimentally validated in BEAS-2B cells after cigarette smoke extract, bleomycin, and combined stimulation. CXCL12 was identified as a core gene for IPF combined with COPD. This gene exhibited high expression levels in the dataset, with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.78, 0.67, 1.00, and 0.86, respectively. Exploratory analysis of CIBERSORT-estimated immune-cell proportions showed significant differences in CD8+ T cells and resting memory CD4+ T cells between the CXCL12-high and CXCL12-low groups. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) indicates that CXCL12 exhibits significantly increased expression in endothelial cells of COPD and fibroblast cells of IPF, providing valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms. Molecular docking results suggested that sitagliptin and LY-294,002 could serve as therapeutic candidates for IPF combined with COPD. Molecular dynamics simulations supported the sustained binding stability of both CXCL12-ligand complexes. In vitro validation further showed that CXCL12 was induced at the mRNA and protein levels after epithelial injury stimulation. CXCL12 plays a key role in the pathogenesis of IPF combined with COPD and holds promise as a potential target for the diagnosis and treatment of this disease.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics Identifies a Causal Immune Gene Panel for Sepsis Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy.
abstract: Sepsis diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of specific biomarkers that reflect immune dysregulation, as conventional markers lack immune specificity and causal grounding. We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization meta-analysis to identify immune phenotypes causally linked to sepsis, with associated genes mapped via multi- -omics annotation. Integrating three GEO datasets (n = 1,039), we constructed a diagnostic panel using six machine learning models, validated its cell-type specificity via singlecell RNA-seq, confirmed protein-level expression using public proteomic datasets, and predicted potential therapeutic compounds targeting the panel genes. We characterized protective and risk immune phenotypes in sepsis, identifying 119 genes enriched in immune-metabolic pathways. Machine learning refined these to a six-gene panel (LY9, CD244, OLFML2B, TMEM59, TBC1D2, and FCER1G), with NNET achieving an AUC of 0.973 (95% CI: 0.951-0.996). Single-cell transcriptomics revealed cell-type-restricted expression, while proteomic data corroborated differential expression of key genes in sepsis-related contexts. Drug repurposing analysis prioritized candidates, highlighting its translational potential. This six-gene panel links immune-based diagnosis directly to therapeutic intervention. The identified genes not only serve as diagnostic biomarkers but also point to repurposable compounds. By connecting causal immune genes to existing drugs, the panel provides a clinical pathway from biomarker detection to targeted sepsis therapy. This study establishes a causally grounded, diagnostically robust six-gene immune panel for sepsis with demonstrated therapeutic potential, offering a translational framework for biomarker-guided diagnosis and targeted immunotherapy.

title: Integrative transcriptomic profiling of the phosphatome identifies DUSP15 as a chromophobe renal cell carcinoma-selective epithelial biomarker associated with an immune-metabolic tumour state.
abstract: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) lacks robust molecular markers and well-defined therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, 265 protein-coding phosphatases were systematically interrogated using pan-cancer transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), cross-cohort evaluation in seven subtype-annotated Gene Expression Omnibus datasets drawn from a ten-dataset compilation, pathway and immune analyses, and two independent single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. DUSP15 emerged as the most chRCC-selective phosphatase (Tau = 0.977) and showed high retrospective discriminative performance both between chRCC and clear-cell and papillary RCC (AUC = 0.976) and between chRCC tumours and adjacent normal kidney tissue (AUC = 0.973) in TCGA. Subtype discrimination was independently reproduced across the GEO cohorts (AUC = 0.837). Transcriptome-wide analyses showed that DUSP15-high tumours were characterised by coordinated enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, MYC target and DNA repair programmes, together with reduced interferon and inflammatory signalling. Immune deconvolution revealed lower regulatory T-cell, dendritic-cell and overall immune enrichment scores, consistent with a relatively immune-poor transcriptional state. Single-cell analyses localised the bulk-tumour DUSP15 signal predominantly to tumour-associated epithelial populations in two independent datasets, with DUSP15 detected in 72.2-83.7% of tumour epithelial cells and pseudobulk abundance ranging from 144.9 to 204.3 counts per million. Expression was substantially lower in immune, stromal, normal renal epithelial and non-chRCC tumour populations. Collectively, these findings identify DUSP15 as a highly selective tumour-epithelial biomarker candidate for chRCC and establish the cellular context of a DUSP15-associated immune-metabolic state with potential diagnostic and biological relevance.

title: Seven-Gene Signature and Immune Microenvironment as Determinants of Survival Rate in Colorectal Carcinoma.
abstract: Backgrounds: Colorectal cancer (CRC) prognosis remains difficult due to molecular heterogeneity and interaction between tumor cells and the immune microenvironment. This study aimed to identify transcriptomic and immune-cell patterns associated with overall survival (OS) and to develop an integrated prognostic model to improve risk stratification. Methods: RNA-sequencing was performed on 131 primary CRC samples and matched normal tissues. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and functionally characterized through gene ontology, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Immune-cell composition was estimated using CIBERSORTx deconvolution and evaluated for its association with OS. Prognostic DEGs were screened using univariate Cox regression and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) analysis to construct a risk score. The model was validated in the Cancer Genome Atlas Database (TCGA)-COAD (colon cancer) and READ (rectal cancer) cohorts. A nomogram integrating molecular and clinicopathological variables were generated. Results: A total of 5589 DEGs were identified between CRC and normal tissues, enriched in pathways related to cell cycle, Tumor Protein P53 (TP53), WNT Family Member (WNT), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK/STAT), calcium signaling, metabolism, and immune regulation. PPI analysis highlighted ten upregulated hub genes involved in mitotic spindle formation and chromosomal stability. Immune infiltration analysys indicated that higher proportions of plasma cells (p = 6.9 × 10- 4), naïve B cells (p = 0.019), resting CD4+ memory T cells (p = 0.02), M0 macrophages (p = 0.0077), and activated dendritic cells (p = 1.89 × 10- 5) were associated with improved OS, whereas monocytes (p = 0.012), neutrophils (p = 0.041), activated mast cells (p = 0.0066), and M2 macrophages (p = 0.014) were linked to poorer survival. A seven-gene signature including aspartate beta-hydroxylase (ASPH), bradykinin receptor B1 (BDKRB1), calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit beta 1 (CACNB1), C-C motif chemokine receptor 8 (CCR8), cyclic nucleotide gated channel subunit alpha 3 (CNGA3), microtubule associated protein 1A (MAP1A) and oxytocin receptor (OXTR) stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significant OS differences. The model demonstrated strong predictive performance (AUC: 0.84 at 1 year) and was validated in TCGA cohorts. Multivariate analysis confirmed the risk score as an independent prognostic factor. The integrated nomogram accurately predicted 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival (C-index = 0.757; 95% CI 0.724-0.791). Conclusions: We developed and validated a seven-gene immune-related prognostic signature that, combined with clinicopathological parameters, provides a robust tool for individualized survival prediction and may guide precision management in CRC patients.

title: Compartment-resolved epithelial and myeloid programs are shared by pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and ischemic stroke.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops within a complex tumor microenvironment characterized by malignant epithelial states, myeloid inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities. Related thrombo-inflammatory transcriptional features have also been observed in ischemic stroke, but whether these diseases share reproducible molecular programs, and how such programs are organized across cellular compartments in PDAC, remains incompletely understood. We integrated transcriptomic datasets from three ischemic stroke cohorts and two paired PDAC tumor-normal cohorts using within-cohort modeling and random-effects meta-analysis. Candidate programs were subsequently investigated using independent bulk transcriptomic, single-cell RNA-sequencing, paired proteomic, spatial transcriptomic, clinical, and human genetic datasets to assess their reproducibility, cellular localization, tumor-microenvironment context, and translational relevance. Iterative quality-control and replication filters identified 46 concordantly altered genes across the analyzed PDAC and ischemic stroke datasets. Six sentinel genes organized this cross-disease transcriptional signal into an epithelial program comprising CEACAM6, ANXA3, and IL1RAP; a myeloid program comprising TREM1 and IL1R2; and a coagulation-associated component represented by F5. All six genes were independently validated in PDAC, while 34 of 36 quantifiable candidate pairs showed concordant transcript-protein changes. Single-cell and spatial analyses localized the epithelial and myeloid programs to distinct malignant and immune compartments within the PDAC microenvironment. After adjustment for inferred cell abundance, the epithelial program remained the most reproducible cross-disease transcriptional feature, whereas the myeloid and coagulation-associated programs showed greater dependence on cellular composition and disease context. External stroke validation was heterogeneous, and survival, protein quantitative trait locus, and colocalization analyses did not support independent prognostic or genetic-causal interpretations. This multi-omic study defines a compartment-resolved cellular framework in PDAC characterized by a stable tumor-associated epithelial program and more context-dependent myeloid and coagulation-associated programs identified through cross-disease analysis with ischemic stroke. These findings provide a mechanistically informed framework for understanding cancer cell-microenvironment relationships and prioritize CEACAM6, ANXA3, IL1RAP, and TREM1 for functional investigation. They should not be interpreted as evidence that these PDAC-associated programs directly cause or mediate ischemic stroke.

title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis with Interpretable Machine Learning Prioritizes Candidate Biomarkers for Bladder Cancer.
abstract: Bladder cancer is the most prevalent malignancy of the urinary tract. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers for bladder cancer through an integrated multi-omics analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and proteomic datasets were analyzed to characterize cellular populations and identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and proteins (DEPs). Candidate genes were prioritized using four machinelearning algorithms, with model interpretation performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was conducted to explore associated pathways, whereas Enrichr/DSigDB enrichment and molecular docking were performed to investigate potential therapeutic compounds and compound-gene interactions. A five-gene SVM model was externally validated in the independent bulk transcriptomic cohort GSE13507. The expression levels of the candidate genes were further evaluated in bladder cancer cell lines. Fifteen major cell populations were identified. Exploratory analyses highlighted endothelial perivascular stromal cells and inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts as cell populations of interest, with predicted intercellular communication patterns suggesting potential roles in the bladder cancer microenvironment. Moreover, 7 genes/proteins showed concordant upregulation and 122 downregulation across all three datasets, and these candidates were subsequently subjected to machine- learning analysis. CFD, WNT2B, MAPK13, ABLIM1, and PRKAR2B were prioritized as five candidate genes for bladder cancer, and their expression patterns and potentially associated pathways were further evaluated in bladder cancer samples and cell lines. Among the four evaluated algorithms, SVM demonstrated the highest reported internal holdout-set AUC of 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and was selected for SHAP interpretation. In the independent GSE13507 cohort, the five-gene SVM model achieved an AUC of 0.815 (95% CI: 0.752-0.877). Molecular docking suggested potential interaction poses between Rifaximin and CFD, and between MAPK13 and NG- 25/XMD13-2. The integration of multi-omics data with an interpretable SHAP-based model provides an exploratory framework for prioritizing candidate bladder cancer biomarkers and generating hypotheses for subsequent biological and clinical validation. This multi-omics study identified candidate biomarkers and exploratory compoundgene associations for bladder cancer. These findings require validation in additional independent multicenter cohorts and functional studies before clinical application.

title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined.
