Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance. We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier. We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4+ TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort. Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

title: Cross-Cohort Transcriptomic and Oral Microbiome Analyses Identify Ferroptosis-Associated Signatures in Periodontitis and Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) have been investigated in relation to inflammation, oral microbial alterations, and iron/redox biology. Whether ferroptosis-associated expression patterns overlap across independently sampled periodontal and cancer cohorts remains uncertain. We characterized these patterns without presuming that the available datasets represent matched individuals or a temporal disease sequence. We analyzed gingival single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE171213), an OSCC discovery expression cohort (GSE30784), and an independent oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma validation cohort (GSE13601). Periodontal microbial functional gene profiles (GSE54290) and a cross-study OSCC 16S abundance resource were examined separately. Analyses included cell annotation, KEGG ferroptosis gene-set scoring, sample- and cell type-level comparisons, differential expression, external transcriptomic signature validation, microbial diversity and abundance analyses, and LPS-stimulated cell-line RT-qPCR and ELISA measurements. The transcriptomic and microbial cohorts were not linked at the individual-patient level. Quality control retained 34,342 cells from 12 gingival samples (four healthy controls [HCs], five PD, and three treated periodontitis [PDT]), assigned to 11 annotated cell populations. Mean sample-level ferroptosis gene-set scores were 0.081 in HC, 0.114 in PD, and 0.076 in PDT; these descriptive scores do not measure ferroptotic cell death. SAT1 showed a positive PD-versus-HC association in cell type pseudobulk analysis (log2 fold change, 0.546; false discovery rate [FDR], 0.012) and positive effects across all three transcriptomic cohorts. A discovery-derived ferroptosis-associated OSCC signature achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.933 in GSE13601. Periodontal functional profiling identified 25 advanced PD-associated annotations (FDR < 0.05), including lower ferrochelatase signals. Cross-study OSCC microbiome analysis found 293 diagnosis-associated features after project adjustment; project-held-out classification yielded an AUC of 0.674. Following lipopolysaccharide stimulation, GPX4, SLC7A11, and FTH1 increased and ACSL4 decreased at the measured mRNA and protein levels in gingival fibroblasts and THP-1-derived macrophages. Independently sampled periodontal and OSCC cohorts show ferroptosis-associated transcriptomic changes, with SAT1 emerging as a cross-cohort candidate. Parallel microbial datasets identify disease-associated functional gene and taxonomic differences but do not demonstrate within-patient host-microbe interactions or causal mediation. LPS-exposed cell-line measurements show expression changes in selected ferroptosis-associated markers, not ferroptotic cell death or functional resistance. The results are exploratory associations; in the absence of direct ferroptosis assays, paired longitudinal cohorts, and prospective clinical validation, they cannot establish a disease-progression mechanism, clinically deployable biomarker or therapeutic efficacy.

title: SerRS2 Identifies an Inflamed-Exhausted Hepatocellular Carcinoma Phenotype with Enhanced DNA-Sensing and Increased Anti-PD-1 Responsiveness.
abstract: Seryl-tRNA synthetase 2 (SerRS2, encoded by SARS2) is a mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase essential for mitochondrial protein translation and homeostasis. Its clinical and immunological significance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. Transcriptomic and clinical data from 371 TCGA-LIHC patients were analyzed to evaluate SerRS2 expression, prognosis, immune infiltration, T-cell exhaustion, and DNA-sensing-related features. Four single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular distribution of SerRS2. Public immunotherapy cohorts were evaluated for associations between SerRS2 expression and immune checkpoint blockade outcomes, and an independent HCC cohort was used for qPCR validation. Group comparisons were performed using Student's t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test, correlations using Pearson or Spearman analyses, and survival outcomes using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the Log rank test, as appropriate. SerRS2 was significantly upregulated in HCC and associated with advanced pathological stage and poorer survival. Elevated SerRS2 expression was consistently associated with increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and exhausted T-cell abundance and positively correlated with PDCD1, TOX, LAG3, HAVCR2, and CTLA4. SerRS2 was also positively associated with cGAS (MB21D1) and DDX41, but not STING1, and SerRS2-high tumors exhibited increased exhaustion and DNA-sensing scores. Collectively, these findings support a SerRS2-associated inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype characterized by increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, T-cell exhaustion-related features, and enrichment of DNA-sensing-related transcriptional programs. Single-cell analyses revealed heterogeneous SerRS2 expression across multiple cellular compartments, supporting its interpretation as a tissue-level rather than tumor-cell-specific signal. In public cross-tumor immunotherapy cohorts, elevated SerRS2 expression was associated with improved outcomes following PD-1 blockade, whereas comparable associations were not consistently observed for PD-L1 or CTLA-4 blockade, suggesting potential relevance of the SerRS2-associated immune phenotype to PD-1 blockade. These immune associations were further supported by qPCR validation in an independent HCC cohort. SerRS2 is associated with an inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype in HCC and may represent a candidate tissue-level biomarker for immune stratification. Its potential relevance to PD-1 blockade warrants prospective validation in HCC-specific immunotherapy cohorts.
